title: Incident triage and decision ladders: rotations, runbooks, game days, and comm templates
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook centralizes our incident triage decision ladders, on-call rotation guidance, concise runbook templates for common production failure modes, a catalogue of game day exercises, and copy-ready customer communication templates. It is intended for on-call responders, incident commanders, SREs, and product stakeholders who participate in incidents or reliability exercises.

Sections in this document:
1) Severity definitions and decision ladder
2) Roles and responsibilities
3) Triage checklist and runbook templates (latency, model failures, auth/keyspace, data exfil risk)
4) Escalation matrix and contact heuristics
5) On-call rotation patterns and handoff checklist
6) Game day catalogue with objectives and expected artifacts
7) Status page and customer communication templates
8) Postmortem checklist and RCA timeline
9) Maintenance and governance

1) Severity definitions and decision ladder

- Severity P0 (Critical): Total outage for Hosted API or Dedicated pools resulting in >30% customer impact across single-region traffic or active Data Plane partition preventing writes for >5 minutes. Immediate IC launch.
- Severity P1 (High): Significant degradation (latency >3x SLO for >10 minutes, or sustained token generation failures) affecting many customers but partial availability remains. IC or escalation to IC depending on impact.
- Severity P2 (Medium): Functionality impaired for a small set of customers or internal degradation (backend job backlog, model-quality regression detected by monitors). Handle during on-call window; consider service owners if persistent.
- Severity P3 (Low): Informational or non-urgent degradations (console UI bug, telemetry gaps). Track as ticket.

Decision ladder (first 30 minutes):
1. Confirm: collect evidence (service status, traces, SLO dashboards, error logs). If P0/P1, create an incident in the tracker and set status to "Investigation".
2. Contain: determine mitigation (traffic cut, fallback model routing, capacity reallocation). Aim to limit customer-visible impact within 15 minutes.
3. Communicate: post internal incident bridge + public status page update (see templates).
4. Restore: route to recovery path (model fallback, region failover, scale-up) and monitor error budget consumption.
5. Post-incident: collect timeline, owners, and begin the postmortem within 72 hours.

2) Roles and responsibilities

- Incident Commander (IC): owns coordination, triage ladder decisions, and external comms approval. Typically an SRE or platform lead during P0/P1.
- Triage Lead: runs initial diagnostics, points to impacted services and suggests mitigations.
- Service Engineers (owners): own technical remediation for their service.
- Communications Lead (Comms): drafts external customer messages and internal summaries.
- Observability Lead: ensures dashboards, SLOs, and trace links are available on the incident page.

3) Triage checklist and runbook templates

General triage checklist (first responder):
- Authenticate to incident tooling and open the incident channel (Slack #inc-<service>-<YYYYMMDD>).
- Snapshot dashboards: SLO overview, per-model latency, per-region error rates, queue/backlog sizes.
- Identify the blast radius: how many customers, routes, and models are affected.
- Check recent deploys and config changes (last 60 minutes).
- If degradation is model-related, verify model variant mappings and KV cache state.

Runbook: high-latency in Hosted API
- Scope: Latency > 2x target p50/p95 for a region.
- Quick checks:
  - Command: curl -s "https://internal-api.redwood.local/health" | jq .status
  - Check GPU saturation: kubectl top pods -n inference | sort -k3 -h
  - Check queue backlog: curl -s https://monitoring.internal/api/queues/summary
- Mitigation options (in order):
  1) Enable burst capacity for affected pool (if available): runbook CLI:
     rwdctl pools scale --pool-id <pool> --burst 50
  2) Toggle fallback routing to lower-latency model variant:
     POST /routing/v1/fallbacks with body {"service":"text-gen","to_variant":"gpt-lite-quant"}
  3) Clear KV cache on targeted hosts (graceful): ssh to host -> supervisorctl restart kv-cache
  4) If saturation persists, perform targeted rolling restart of inference nodes (see infra runbook).
- Validation: monitor p95 and token error rate; confirm <10% customer impact remaing.

Runbook: model-evaluation/regression trigger (quality guardrail)
- Scope: automated evals show significant regression vs baseline for production prompt set (>5% metric drop).
- Quick checks: verify eval job id, compare to prior baselines, check model version and rollout percentage.
- Mitigation options:
  1) Immediate: rollback rollout to previous model: rwdctl rollout rollback --model-id <model> --to-version <vX>
  2) Quarantine model variant in routing table.
  3) Initiate targeted re-eval on small customer prompt set to confirm impact.
- Post-incident: ensure model onboarding checklist is updated (check quantization profile, sampling defaults, prompt templates).

Runbook: auth/keyspace failure (middleware tokens invalid)
- Scope: API auth failures across region or failed JWKS retrieval.
- Quick checks: verify KMS/JWKS availability endpoints, recent cert rotations, error logs show 401/403.
- Mitigation:
  1) Fallback to cached JWKS if allowed and rotate; update status page.
  2) If cert caused rotation, rollback the cert change or re-provision in KMS.
  3) Notify security if key compromise suspected.

4) Escalation matrix and contact heuristics

Escalation order (rough): on-call engineer -> service owner -> platform SRE -> IC -> vp/platform (for P0 lasting >60m). Use callout numbers only for P0s. If multiple teams are affected, IC calls cross-team leads.

Escalation heuristics:
- If customer-impacting and not resolving within 15m, escalate to platform SRE.
- If mitigation requires infra operator with cloud-console access, page infra on-call immediately.
- If security-sensitive (data exfiltration, credentials), page Security and pause external comms until triage confirms scope.

5) On-call rotation patterns and handoff checklist

Recommended rotation patterns:
- Primary/Secondary 1-week rotations for Platform SREs (primary handles incidents; secondary supports).
- Paging window: 08:00–20:00 local weekdays; weekend coverage: 24/7 primary with a lighter secondary shift.
- Shadowing: new on-call should shadow for at least one rotation or two game days.

Handoff checklist (to be posted in rotation channel):
1. Current active incidents and status.
2. Known degradations and work in progress.
3. Paging thresholds and escalation contacts.
4. Token/key rotations happening in next 48h.
5. Planned deploys during on-call window.

6) Game day catalogue (exercises designed to validate our runbooks)

Game day #1: Cross-region failover
- Objective: verify we can fail over traffic between us-east and eu-west with <5m customer impact.
- Participants: Platform SRE, Networking, Infra, Product owner.
- Steps: disable region route, monitor fallback routing, measure failover time, validate data-plane sync.
- Expected artifacts: timeline, playbooks exercised, action items.

Game day #2: Model-fallback and quality regression simulation
- Objective: confirm that rollback and routing to quantized variant preserves availability and meets basic quality thresholds.
- Steps: simulate degraded model, initiate fallback routing, run smoke evals against production prompt set.

Game day #3: Status page and customer comms rehearsal
- Objective: practise drafting public messages, internal incident notes, and exec briefing within 30 minutes.
- Steps: simulate P1 incident, have Comms draft message, route for legal/PR quick review, publish to staging status page.

7) Status page and customer communication templates

Public status page template (short):
- Title: "Degraded performance for Redwood API (region: eu-west)"
- Status: Investigating / Identified / Monitoring / Resolved
- Impact: A subset of requests to text-generation endpoints returning higher latency or errors.
- Time detected: 2025-02-11T09:18:00Z
- Next update: 2025-02-11T09:40:00Z
- Mitigation: Routing to alternate variant (in progress).
- Contact: support@redwood.ai (for urgent incidents)

Detailed customer email template (when P1/P0):
Subject: Incident update — Redwood inference (short summary)
Body:
  Hello,

  We are investigating increased latency affecting text generation in eu-west. Our teams have identified a remediation path and are routing traffic to an alternate model variant. We will provide another update within 30 minutes and are prioritizing restoration.

  Best regards,
  Redwood Support

Internal Slack status snippet for #inc-<service> channel:
  [IC] P1 — Investigating increased latency in eu-west. Mitigation: fallback routing to gpt-lite-quant initiated at 09:22Z. Monitoring p95 and error-rate. Owner: @service-owner.

8) Postmortem checklist and RCA timeline

Postmortem must include:
- Executive summary (1 paragraph).
- Impact statement (customers, capacity, financial if known).
- Timeline with minute-level granularity for first 60 minutes, then 15-min granularity thereafter.
- Root cause(s) and contributing factors (people, process, code, infra).
- Mitigations and short-term fixes applied during incident.
- Action items, owners, and ETA (no more than 3 high-priority action items).
- Follow-up validation plan (how we will verify fixes).

RCA cadence:
- T+24h: initial timeline, owners assigned, and incident page locked for edits.
- T+72h: draft postmortem due.
- T+7d: final postmortem published and review meeting scheduled.

9) Maintenance and governance

Runbook lifecycle:
- Runbooks reviewed quarterly by owners. Game days should exercise at least one runbook per quarter.
- Any runbook change must include a short changelog entry and reviewer sign-off.

SLOs and error budgets (reference values):
- API availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for hosted endpoints.
- Model response latency p95: <450ms for small prompt workloads.
- Alert thresholds mapped to severity in our alerts catalog.

Appendix: Useful commands and links
- Create incident: rwd-incident create --service <service> --severity P1 --summary "<short summary>"
- Incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood.local/
- Oncall schedule: https://rota.redwood.local/
- Observability dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/llm-platform

If you are an on-call responder and this document is missing a case you encountered, add a short entry to the runbook and tag the owner for review.
